strategy_title: Persistent Grid-Stride Loop Causes Massive Instruction Blowup
strategy_description: Applying a persistent grid-stride while-loop to a sub-wave kernel caused a 99x regression. The implementation kept the original grid (512 CTAs) unchanged instead of reducing it to NUM_SMS (132) CTAs, so each of the 512 CTAs still ran the while-loop, iterating over all tiles and executing ~767x more instructions (91M vs 119K). The strategy is sound in principle but requires the grid to be set to exactly NUM_SMS CTAs; if the grid is not reduced, the persistent loop multiplies work instead of redistributing it.

    num_sms = num_programs(0)  # must equal NUM_SMS=132
    total_tiles = cdiv(ynumel, YBLOCK) * cdiv(xnumel, XBLOCK)
    tile_id = pid

        # compute offsets from tile_id
        # load/store one tile
        tile_id += num_sms

# ACTUAL (BROKEN) AFTER: grid unchanged at 512, loop runs on all 512 CTAs
grid = (cdiv(xnumel, 128), cdiv(ynumel, 8))  # still (1, 512)!
kernel[grid](..., YBLOCK=8, XBLOCK=128)  # each CTA loops over ALL tiles
applicable_when: Kernel has waves_per_sm < 0.5, achieved occupancy < 25%, grid_size < 2*sm_count, and duration is dominated by launch overhead / instruction-cache cold-start (CPIStall rule triggered, kernel duration < 10us).
do_not_apply_when: The grid is not simultaneously reduced to NUM_SMS CTAs — if the original grid is kept while adding the while-loop, every CTA will iterate over all tiles, causing O(grid_size/NUM_SMS) instruction blowup. Also avoid when the kernel already has high occupancy or is memory-bandwidth bound.
framework_notes: In Triton, the persistent grid must be launched as grid=(NUM_SMS,) with a 1D program_id(0). Using tl.num_programs(0) to get num_sms only works correctly if the grid is actually set to NUM_SMS. The diff shows the grid was left as (cdiv(xnumel,128), cdiv(ynumel,8))=(1,512) while the kernel body was rewritten to use program_id(0) and a while-loop — this is the implementation flaw.

strategy_title: Persistent Tile Loop Broken by Mismatched Grid Launch
strategy_description: The persistent kernel body was correctly rewritten to use a while-loop over tile_id, but the launcher was not updated to match: it still used the old 2D grid formula (cdiv(xnumel,128), cdiv(ynumel,8)) and passed YBLOCK=8, XBLOCK=128 instead of the intended YBLOCK=32, XBLOCK=16. This caused the kernel to launch 512 blocks each iterating over a vastly larger number of tiles than intended, inflating executed instructions from ~119K to ~85M and duration from 3 µs to 271 µs — a 96x regression. The strategy of persistent tile scheduling is sound for sub-wave kernels, but the grid size and block tile parameters in the launcher must be consistent with the tile decomposition inside the kernel body.

fast_pseudocode:
# CORRECT persistent version (strategy is right, launcher must match)
@triton.jit
def kernel(in_ptr0, out_ptr0, ynumel, xnumel, YBLOCK: tl.constexpr, XBLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    pid = tl.program_id(0)
    grid_size = tl.num_programs(0)
    num_xtiles = tl.cdiv(xnumel, XBLOCK)   # e.g. cdiv(9,16)=1
    num_ytiles = tl.cdiv(ynumel, YBLOCK)   # e.g. cdiv(4096,32)=128
    num_tiles = num_xtiles * num_ytiles     # 128
    tile_id = pid
    while tile_id < num_tiles:
        ytile = tile_id // num_xtiles
        xtile = tile_id % num_xtiles
        yindex = ytile*YBLOCK + tl.arange(0, YBLOCK)[:, None]
        xindex = xtile*XBLOCK + tl.arange(0, XBLOCK)[None, :]
        ...
        tl.store(...)
        tile_id += grid_size

# LAUNCHER must match kernel tile params:
XBLOCK, YBLOCK = 16, 32
num_xtiles = cdiv(xnumel, XBLOCK)   # 1
num_ytiles = cdiv(ynumel, YBLOCK)   # 128
num_tiles = num_xtiles * num_ytiles  # 128
grid_size = min(NUM_SMS, num_tiles)  # 128
kernel[grid_size,](arg_0, arg_1, ynumel, xnumel, YBLOCK=YBLOCK, XBLOCK=XBLOCK)
applicable_when: Kernel has sub-wave grid (waves_per_sm < 0.5), very low achieved occupancy (<15%), both compute and memory SOL <10%, and SOLBottleneck + AchievedOccupancy rules triggered. Total tile count is small (< 2x SM count).
do_not_apply_when: The launcher grid and kernel tile parameters are not updated atomically together — mismatching them causes catastrophic instruction count explosion. Do not apply when the kernel already has waves_per_sm > 1 or when the total work is large enough to fill the GPU without a persistent loop.
framework_notes: In Triton, the persistent loop uses tl.program_id(0) and tl.num_programs(0) for 1D grid. The launcher must pass a 1D grid tuple (grid_size,) and explicit XBLOCK/YBLOCK constexpr values matching the tile decomposition inside the kernel. Mismatching XBLOCK/YBLOCK between launcher and kernel body causes the while-loop to iterate far more times than intended, multiplying instruction count by (wrong_tiles / correct_tiles).
